ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a transition-state structure containing a bicyclic/chair-like carbon skeleton; on the left there is a negatively charged oxygen connected to the central carbon; the central carbon is also connected to an ethoxy substituent labeled OEt; below, there is a Br connected to a skeleton carbon. There are also several curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring these arrows. Reasoning count: count non-hydrogen bonds by components. The C–C bonds of the carbon skeleton, including the connection from the central carbon to the skeleton, total 10; the left O−–C connection is 1; the C–O bond from the central carbon to OEt is 1; after expanding OEt, it also contains two bonds, O–C and C–C, totaling 2; the C–Br bond is 1. Therefore the total is 10 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 15.

raw_record.question_text: In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen. Disregard arrows and consider all components present in the transition-state structure.

method.method_draft: First describe the drawing and ignore all curved arrows. Count the non-H bonds by components: (i) the carbon framework in the bicyclic/chair portion, including the central carbon-to-framework connection, gives 10 C–C bonds; (ii) the left alkoxide connection O−–C gives 1 bond; (iii) the drawn C–O bond to the OEt substituent gives 1 bond; (iv) expanding OEt adds O–C and C–C, 2 bonds; (v) the C–Br bond adds 1 bond. Add these component counts: 10 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 15.

method.method_draft: Reconstruct the heavy-atom graph from the image.
